 Order

T his i s second application under section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure, for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant relating to FIR/Crime No.146/2021 dated 11.03.2023 registered at Police Station- Omti, District- Jabalpur, for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.
His previous application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 27.04.2023 in M.Cr.C. No.16752/2023.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 15.03.2023.
He submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He further submits that challan has been filed.
The applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Trial will take considerable time to conclude.
Upon these submissions, learned counsel prays that the applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the contrary, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.
Prosecution case is that applicant was charge-sheeted in a summary case in which he was sentenced to pay fine amount of Rs.10,000/-.
He deposited the fine amount through online mode by his counsel, but after two months it was found that the amount was not deposited and the receipt filed by the applicant was fake.
Looking to the nature and circumstances of the crime, I find it appropriate to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail subject to payment of fine amount of Rs.10,000/-, if not paid in the concerned summary case and upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
